headline: Common Mistakes in Bathroom Accessibility Modifications
articleBody: When modifying a bathroom for accessibility, it’s easy to make choices that seem helpful but actually create new problems or simply don't work for the user. One of the biggest mistakes is installing grab bars or other accessories without checking for proper wall backing. You need solid support behind those fixtures, otherwise, they can pull right out of the wall when weight is applied, leading to falls. Another common misstep is choosing a layout that blocks maneuvering space. What looks good on paper might not allow enough room for a wheelchair or walker to turn, or for a caregiver to assist. Always consider the actual circulation path! Using slippery surfaces is also a frequent mistake. While certain tiles might look great, if they become slick when wet, they're a hazard for anyone with limited mobility. Opt for slip-resistant flooring. Lastly, don't make changes that *look* accessible but don’t fit the user’s actual transfer and reach needs. Every person's requirements are unique, so what works for one might not work for another. It's really worth getting professional advice to ensure the modifications truly enhance usability and safety.
